messages:
Mia: heads-up — I hit a hard hang when running the sample app locally. async requests stall whenever the SDK refreshes auth tokens.
Devon: can you paste the stack or a repro?
Mia: stack looks like asyncio stuck on a threadpool call, but we only call httpx.AsyncClient. quick paste: 
```
  File "uvicorn/workers.py", line 65, in run
    asyncio.run(self.main())
  File "asyncio/runners.py", line 44, in run
    loop.run_until_complete(main)
  File "asyncio/base_events.py", line 616, in run_until_complete
    return future.result()
  File "site-packages/httpx/_client.py", line 1200, in aconnect
    response = sync_client.request(...)
```
Mia: obviously edited down but you can see a sync call in httpx internals.
Ben: that usually means something synchronous is being invoked from an auth hook or middleware. are you using a custom auth that calls `requests` or does sync I/O?
Mia: yes — our onboarding sample still used the older helper that does a `requests.post` to refresh tokens (copied from a sync example). we create a global AsyncClient at import-time too.
Olivia: two things: (1) creating AsyncClient at import time -> potential event loop mismatch if created before uvicorn spawns workers, (2) sync token refresh in auth callback blocks the loop via thread executor. also saw contextvar values lost when we spawn threads for background tasks.
Devon: can you paste the auth snippet?
Mia: sure:
```python
# auth.py
def get_token():
    resp = requests.post("https://auth.internal/refresh", json={"refresh": REF})  # blocking
    return resp.json()["access_token"]

async def fetch():
    client = httpx.AsyncClient()
    client.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {get_token()}"
    await client.get("https://api.internal/foo")
```
Mia: this is dumb but was copy/pasted from the quickstart.
Ben: yep, that will deadlock under load. For async usage you must make the refresh async and dedupe concurrent refreshes with a lock. also avoid creating AsyncClient at import time — do it in startup and call `await client.__aenter__()` or use the async context manager in your app lifecycle.
Olivia: another subtlety: our SDK retry middleware will call the auth callback again on 401s; if the callback is sync it double-wraps into threadpool and you get nested blocking calls. also FYI there is a typing oddity: some async methods are annotated as returning `Response` instead of `httpx.Response | Awaitable[httpx.Response]` which confuses mypy/IDE; that made it easy for folks to accidentally write sync helper functions.
Sam: filed GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/2421 with a tiny repro and suggested fix (async token helper + refresh lock).
Devon: we should ship an `AsyncAuth` helper in the SDK that provides: async refresh function signature, an internal asyncio.Lock to dedupe refresh, and a sync shim for sync users. Add builtin examples in the sample-apps repo showing correct usage with FastAPI/uvicorn startup.
Mia: trying the quick patch now: replace `requests.post` with `await httpx.AsyncClient().post(...)` inside an async `ensure_token()` and create client inside `startup` — will report back. :crossed_fingers:
ci-bot: created issue #2421 and kicked off CI for the sample-apps PR (run #3482).
Mia: patch confirmed — switching to async refresh + startup-scoped AsyncClient resolved the hang in our env. thanks! :thumbsup:
Olivia: opened an internal task to add an `auth_async_helper` and update quickstarts so we don't ship sync anti-patterns. also adding a small mypy test for AsyncClient typing in CI.
Ben: cc @DevEx — might be a good follow-up doc blurb about common sync/async pitfalls when moving examples between the sync and async SDKs.
Mia: agreed. saving the repro and notes to the sample-apps issue.
Devon: nice — closing loop. if anyone hits other event-loop mismatches ping me.
